reason: The cited evidence shows that c/a ratio in transformative HEAs changes with processing and that lower c/a promotes pyramidal slip and twinning, but it does not address time-dependent plastic deformation (creep) resistance, multilayer coatings, or optimization of c/a ratio for improved creep properties.
premises: c/a ratio of ε-phase in transformative HEAs can be altered by processing and deformation
Lower than ideal c/a ratio promotes non-basal pyramidal slip and deformation twinning
Non-basal pyramidal slip and deformation twinning accommodate strain and improve work hardening
Optimizing c/a ratio in ε-phase will improve resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation (creep)
These mechanisms apply to high-entropy-alloy multilayer protective coatings
